title: Improved Mixing Constants for Reverse Cycle Walking
summary: RCW has an explicit logarithmic-step variation-distance bound toward uniform permutations; the open task is to improve its constants while retaining the same guarantee.

formal_statement.body: For the reverse cycle walking (RCW) algorithm on a set of size $N_S$, existing analysis provides explicit constants $k_1$ and $k_2$ such that, after $k=k_1\log(N_S)$ steps, the distribution $\nu_k^{\mathrm{rcw}}$ satisfies $\lVert\nu_k^{\mathrm{rcw}}-\mu_S\rVert\le N_S^{-k_2}$, where $\mu_S$ is uniform over permutations of the set. Derive quantitatively improved explicit constants while preserving a mixing and variation-distance guarantee of this form.

scope.domain: Markov-chain mixing analysis of reverse cycle walking on finite permutation spaces.
parameters: k_1: multiplier in the logarithmic step count
k_2: exponent governing the variation-distance bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive quantitatively improved explicit constants while retaining a mixing and variation-distance guarantee of the stated form.

citations.label: Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications

progress.summary: The paper customizes the analysis for RCW by providing explicit constants and new proofs of two key lemmas. It presents these constants as a starting point and states that further reduction is possible.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications
